comparison: Both evaluate the NGS validation and CRISPR mutagenic efficacy (C4, C21-C25) and reach the same SUPPORTED conclusion. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative metrics and off-target analysis, while peer reviewers highlight the 60-92% inactivation rates. Complete agreement on technical validity.

Both address gene selection criteria (C2, C3, C19, C20). OpenEval finds the selection well-justified and SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about incomplete characterization of gene features (maternal transcripts, genetic compensation) that could affect crispant phenotypes and interpretation.

Both evaluate RT-qPCR gene expression findings (C32-C39) and reach SUPPORTED conclusions. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical methods and consistent patterns, while peer reviewers emphasize correlation between molecular and phenotypic data. Both acknowledge caveats about whole-body samples and genetic compensation.

Both assess survival/lethality phenotypes (C40-C43) and reach SUPPORTED conclusions. OpenEval describes severe lethality as important functional validation, while peer reviewers accept mortality findings without challenge, treating them as valid observations of gene functional importance.

Both evaluate overall reproducibility and platform success (C60, C61) with SUPPORTED conclusions. OpenEval emphasizes reproducibility across clutches and universal adult phenotypes, while peer reviewers strongly affirm the approach as compelling and feasible with convincing data.

Both address larval osteoblast imaging (C26, C27), but peer result R2 also includes mineralization data (C28-C31). OpenEval rates findings SUPPORTED with adequate statistical power, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to lack of body size normalization and high variability affecting interpretation.

OpenEval R4 addresses mineralization findings (C28-C31) rating them SUPPORTED despite acknowledged high variability. Peer R2 covers these same claims plus osteoblast data (C26, C27) but rates UNCERTAIN due to normalization concerns and variability, showing disagreement on confidence level for larval phenotypes.

Both address adult morphological observations (C44-C47). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes lack of statistical testing for qualitative observations limits conclusions. Peer R5 also covers microCT data (C48-C51) and rates all adult phenotypes SUPPORTED, viewing them as the most robust findings.

OpenEval R8 addresses microCT findings (C48-C51) rating them SUPPORTED with appropriate quantitative analysis. Peer R5 covers these claims along with morphological data (C44-C47) and strongly affirms adult skeletal phenotypes as SUPPORTED, emphasizing them as the most convincing and reproducible results.

OpenEval R9 synthesizes RT-qPCR findings (C8, C34, C35, C38, C39) focusing on biomarker potential and rates SUPPORTED. Peer R3 covers the broader gene expression dataset (C32-C39) also rating SUPPORTED. Both note the correlation between molecular and phenotypic data, with overlapping claims showing agreement.

Both address background literature and crispant validation precedents (C16, C17, C18). OpenEval R14 covers broader background (C1, C9-C18) rating all SUPPORTED. Peer R8 focuses on prior crispant validation and rates SUPPORTED, accepting the methodological foundation without challenge.

OpenEval R11 evaluates literature citations contextualizing findings (C52-C57) and rates SUPPORTED, noting these are supporting citations rather than novel findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these literature comparison claims.

OpenEval R12 addresses genetic compensation mechanisms (C58, C59) and rates UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental evidence. While peer reviewers mention genetic compensation as a caveat in R3 and R7, no specific peer result focuses on evaluating these mechanistic claims.

OpenEval R13 evaluates comprehensive methodological details (C62-C76) rating them SUPPORTED with appropriate protocols and statistical approaches. Peer reviewers discuss specific methodological concerns (e.g., normalization in R2) but no peer result systematically evaluates the full methods claims.
